title: Agentic Attack Index incident record
description: One real-world incident of an AI-agent-executed or AI-orchestrated cyberattack. Every factual field must be backed by a cited, resolvable source; unknown values stay null/empty.

id.description: Stable kebab-case slug. Permanent: it is the citation key. Never renamed or recycled.

summary.description: Defensive-framing summary at lifecycle level. No exploit code, payloads, prompts, or step-by-step offensive instructions.

date_disclosed.description: Date the incident was first publicly disclosed (ISO 8601).

status.description: confirmed = multiple independent or first-party confirmation; reported = public reporting not independently confirmed; test-eval = lab test or evaluation, not a real-world attack.

confidence.description: primary = first-party/primary sourcing; secondary = secondhand reporting; unverified = single unconfirmed source.

models.description: Specific model names as stated by sources (e.g. a versioned model identifier). Empty if sources do not name a model.

model_families.description: Controlled vocabulary of model families involved. Use 'other' when sources name no covered family.

actor.description: Threat actor as stated by sources. 'Unknown' is a valid value; never attribute beyond sources.

autonomy_pct.description: Percentage of the operation performed autonomously by the AI agent, only if a source states it. null when unstated.

autonomy_level.description: Agentic Autonomy Level — a discrete class for how much of the operation the AI executed without human intervention, assessed from sources. 'not-applicable' for incidents where the AI is the victim (e.g. agent-hijack) rather than the operator.

guardrail_bypass.description: How the model's safety controls were circumvented or sidestepped, per sources.

ai_role.description: Editorial assessment of how central AI actually was to the incident — a skepticism axis independent of status. 'incidental' where sources indicate AI was a productivity aid rather than load-bearing; 'disputed' where sources conflict or a vendor's framing is contested.

related.description: Ids of other records in this dataset related to this one (same disclosure/report, campaign, actor, or closely related technique/product). Every id must resolve to an existing record; enforced by validate.

mitigations.description: Defensive measures or detections as described by sources — defensive framing only, no offensive detail.

record_status.description: Lifecycle of this dataset record itself (not the incident). Omitted means 'active'. 'disputed' = sources conflict or the framing is contested; 'retracted' = withdrawn but kept for citation stability; 'superseded' = replaced by another record (set superseded_by).

superseded_by.description: Id of the record that supersedes this one. Required when record_status is 'superseded'; must resolve to an existing record (enforced by validate).

revisions.description: Append-only audit trail of material corrections or retractions. Routine edits just bump last_updated; use this for substantive changes reviewers should see.

orgs_affected.description: Number of organizations affected, only if a source states it.

records_exfiltrated.description: Number of records exfiltrated, only if a source states it.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes of targets, as stated by sources.

geo.description: Map points for the tracker. Omit geo entirely when no cited source states a location. Each point carries an explicit, validated basis (why it exists) and the publisher that stated it; targets.countries is never turned into points.

lifecycle_phases.description: Attack lifecycle phases observed, per sources. Descriptive only — no operational detail.

mappings.description: External framework IDs exactly as published — never invent an ID. mitre_atlas preferred for AI-native techniques; mitre_attack for traditional TTPs.

owasp_llm.description: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications IDs, e.g. LLM01.

owasp_asi.description: OWASP Agentic Security Initiative (ASI) threat IDs, e.g. T1. Distinct from the LLM Top 10 — use owasp_llm for those.

impact.description: Stated impact (financial, data, operational), only as sources describe it.

sources.description: Every record needs at least one resolvable source. No source, no record.

archive_url.description: Optional archival snapshot (e.g. Wayback Machine) so the record survives link rot. Must resolve independently of url.

role.description: origin = where the attack came from (by the stated basis); target = where it was aimed.

basis.description: Why this point exists, as a cited source states it (see taxonomy/geo-basis.yml). A state sponsor is not an operator location.

attributed_by.description: Publisher that stated the basis. Must exactly equal a sources[].publisher on this record (enforced by validate).

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the point. null only for a non-country region centroid (illustrative: true).

illustrative.description: true when the point is a country/region centroid rather than a precise, source-stated location. Required true for every basis except stated-location, which requires false.
